data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A 44-comparator 13-input sorting network exists and can be constructed by extending a known optimal 12-input network (S(12)=39 comparators) with a 5-comparator insertion sequence for the 13th channel, because the information-theoretic insertion lower bound for one new channel into a sorted 12-element sequence is ceil(log2(13))=4 and the slack of one extra comparator (39+5=44<45) suffices to satisfy the 0-1 principle across all 8192 binary vectors.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Every known optimal 12-input network requires at least 6 comparators to insert the 13th channel while satisfying the full 0-1 principle, making the achievable minimum 39+6=45 or worse.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The information-theoretic lower bound of ceil(log2(13))=4 applies to sequential binary insertion, not to parallel comparator networks where the 0-1 principle demands simultaneous correctness across all binary vectors, so even 5 is insufficient and the real minimum insertion is 7+.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A 44-comparator 13-input network exists but is structurally inseparable from the 12-input optimum \u2014 i.e., it cannot be decomposed as optimal-12-plus-5-comparator-insertion, so this specific search strategy finds nothing even though the target exists.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Take any known optimal 12-input network (39 comparators, e.g., from the SAT-settled construction). Append channel 12 as initially unconstrained. Enumerate candidate 5-comparator insertion sequences where each comparator involves channel 12 paired with some channel 0..11, interleaved arbitrarily with the existing 39. For each candidate, run the full 0-1 verification: all 2^13=8192 binary vectors through the 44-comparator network in milliseconds of pure Python. The bounded search space is at most (number of ways to place 5 comparators involving channel 12 among 44 positions) \u00d7 (comparator partner choices), which is small enough for exhaustive enumeration under a fixed budget of ~10^7 candidate evaluations. If any candidate passes all 8192 vectors, a verified 44-comparator network is produced.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
